svg.title: How the kit works: two threads and their messages
svg.desc: Animated diagram. code.ts runs on Figma's main thread (the figma API, no DOM); ui.html runs in an iframe (the DOM, no figma object) with the kit's tokens, components and runtime blocks. installKitWindow() opens the window hidden at 320 × 360. The runtime sends kit:ready { protocol: 1 }, code.ts answers kit:init { mode, chrome, bounds, size, … }, the runtime measures the content and sends kit:resize { width: 320, height: 237, … }, and code.ts calls figma.ui.resize and shows the window at that size. (That this removes a blank or unfitted flash in Figma itself is still to be re-checked in a Figma run.) Clicking Create sends the demo's create-shapes message; code.ts answers created and selection, the status grows to two lines, and one more kit:resize grows the window to 245. Sizes are those of the starter in the kit's browser preview.

g.text: From 1 to 50, placed in a row.
1 · Opens hidden, then sized by the kit’s messages
The runtime measures [data-kit-root]; code.ts applies the size.
2 · Shown once it has fitted its content
Hidden until then, so it shouldn’t flash blank or jump (to re-check in Figma).
3 · Your messages use the same channel
Any type that isn’t kit:*, typed like kit.d.ts types the kit’s.
4 · The content grew a line, so the window follows
A ResizeObserver refits it: one more kit:resize.
kit:ready, kit:init, kit:resize, kit:fit: the kit’s own (kit.d.ts)
any other type: yours (here, the starter’s demo)
